entry_state: Conversion inducements use the binding amendment and legal release dates; delivery can be a later transfer within equity. Cash-flow hedge reserves track cumulative effectiveness and leave equity according to the hedged transaction, independently of derivative settlement. Fair-value adjustments change subsequent effective interest. Excluded option time value needs separate actual and aligned valuations, transaction or period treatment, and cumulative measurement. The mismatched-strike example has introduced its two intrinsic values and conditional reserve formulas; its final transaction remains to be read.
exit_state: Actual and hypothetical options retain separate payoffs and component values; a matched collar can carry signed reserves despite zero initial net premium. Rebalancing preserves cumulative gains and each item or instrument designation origin. Added derivative carrying value includes acquisition cost, which is not a hedge gain. Instrument reduction has begun: the removed fraction retains earlier gains but its subsequent changes enter earnings; the general history formulas continue next.
findings: The mismatched-strike example demonstrates that a balanced inventory and equity statement can still measure the wrong hedged risk.
The collar distinguishes two actual contracts and gross cash flows from net reserves. Its separate finite valuation witnesses are explicitly not estimated probabilities or a joint forecast model.
Repeated item additions reverse prior ineffectiveness under cumulative measurement. Added instruments distinguish purchased value from subsequent gain, including opposite asset and liability signs.
Instrument reduction uses the removed instrument fraction and its own value, rather than a proportion of aggregate nominal quantity. No new confirmed defect in these six pages.
